message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Upload to PyPi

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
        # IMPORTANT: this permission is mandatory for trusted publishing
        id-token: write
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        fetch-depth: 0
        fetch-tags: true
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: 3.9
    - name: Set up uv
      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
    - name: Cache uv dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/uv
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-uv-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-uv-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        uv pip install --system '.[build]'
    - name: Build a binary wheel
      run: |
        python sup3r/utilities/_clean_readme.py README.rst
        python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist/ .
    - name: Check distribution files
      run: |
        twine check dist/*
    - name: Publish
      uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1",
  "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly fetches build dependencies via `uv pip install --system '.[build]'` on every release/dispatch run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern applies because dependency fetching is repeatable and pyproject.toml provides a cache input; a measured experiment for dependency caching reported ~9% elapsed savings. Adding an actions/cache step for the uv cache, keyed on pyproject.toml with restore keys, preserves all build/publish steps, the id-token write permission, and required checks, while reducing repeated download time. No permissions are weakened and no new network targets or privileged actions are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
